suppress.notes:
FALSE POSITIVE. Dependency-Check matches io.projectreactor.netty:reactor-netty-core to cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty by version number alone (1.2.18 / 1.3.x), and then attaches the entire Netty advisory history to it -- 60+ CVEs per service, including CVE-2019-20444/ 20445 and the netty-codec-http request-smuggling family. The report itself marks the match as low confidence. reactor-netty is a separate Spring project artifact and is not the software those advisories describe.
Scoped to the reactor-netty-core jar by file path on purpose: the real io.netty:* jars it pulls in are NOT suppressed and must keep reporting. Those are managed by the Spring Boot BOM.
SCOPE NARROWED 2026-08-31: only mas-api-gateway still ships reactor-netty. NDI never used its webflux starter at all (removed), and Quarrying-Lease now runs WebClient on JdkClientHttpConnector with spring-boot-starter-reactor-netty excluded, so the jar is gone from both. The gateway cannot follow them: Spring Cloud Gateway's WebSocketClient bean comes from NettyConfiguration, and without it the context fails to start outright (verified - filteringWebHandler -> websocketRoutingFilter -> no WebSocketClient bean). This rule is kept in the other repos as a safety net in case a webflux starter returns transitively; it currently matches nothing there, which is the intended state.

FALSE POSITIVE. CVE-2018-1258 is an authorization bypass affecting Spring Security 5.0.5 used together with Spring Framework 5.0.5, fixed in 5.0.6 in 2018. The NVD entry carries an open-ended version range, so Dependency-Check re-flags it against every later release indefinitely. Nothing in MAS runs an affected version -- the estate is on Spring Security 7.0.x.
Affects all backends: core, web, oauth2-resource-server and crypto jars.
